{{Short description|none}}
[[File:Vuelta espana 2022 CRI Elche Alicante-190 - 52325945109.jpg|thumb|right|[[Remco Evenepoel]] wearing the Red Jersey at the [[2022 Vuelta a España]]]]
The [[Vuelta a España]] is an annual [[Road bicycle racing|road bicycle race]]. Established in 1935 by the Spanish newspaper ''Informaciones'', the Vuelta is one of cycling's three "[[Grand Tour (cycling)|Grand Tours]]", along with the [[Tour de France]] and the [[Giro d'Italia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uci.ch/templates/UCI/UCI1/layout.asp?MenuId=MTk0Nw&LangId=1 |title=FAQ |publisher=Union Cycliste Internationale |access-date=17 August 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090723024909/http://www.uci.ch/templates/UCI/UCI1/layout.asp?MenuId=MTk0Nw&LangId=1 |archive-date=23 July 2009 }}</ref> Initially, the race was held in April/May, but in 1995 it was moved to September.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cyclingnews.com/features/did-the-vueltas-date-change-hurt-the-race|title=Did the Vuelta's date change hurt the race?|work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=27 February 2008|access-date=1 May 2011 }}</ref> The race usually covers approximately 3,500 kilometres (2,200&nbsp;mi), although this has varied, passing through Spain and countries with a close proximity in Europe.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://autobus.cyclingnews.com/road/2009/vuelta09/ |title=Vuelta 2009: Easy start, tough ending |work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |access-date=13 September 2010 |first=Bjorn |last=Hakke }}</ref> The race is broken into day-long segments called stages. Individual finishing times for each stage are totalled to determine the overall winner at the end of the race. The course changes every year, but has traditionally finished in [[Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailypeloton.com/displayarticle.asp?pk=13880 |title=2009 Vuelta a España — 64th Edition of the Tour of Spain |publisher=Daily Peloton |date=19 December 2008 |access-date=13 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101214145350/http://dailypeloton.com/displayarticle.asp?pk=13880 |archive-date=14 December 2010 }}</ref>

Individual times to finish each stage are totalled to determine the winner of the general classification at the end of the race. The rider with the lowest aggregate time at the end of each day wears the leader's jersey. Since 2010 this has been a [[red jersey]]; previously it was gold.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cyclingnews.com/news/vuelta-start-in-seville-for-2010 |title=Vuelta start in Seville for 2010  |work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=16 September 2009 |access-date=2 May 2011 |first=Richard |last=Tyler }}</ref> Other classifications have been calculated: those still in use are the [[points classification in the Vuelta a España|points classification]], in 2010 represented by a green jersey; the [[Mountains classification in the Vuelta a España|mountains classification]], in 2010 represented by a blue dotted jersey; and the [[Young rider classification in the Vuelta a España|young rider classification]], in 2019 represented by a white jersey.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.velonation.com/News/ID/1735/Millar-takes-Vuelta-TT-Valverde-seals-overall.aspx |title=Millar takes Vuelta TT, Valverde seals overall |publisher=Velo Nation |date=19 September 2009 |access-date=2 May 2011 |first=Bjorn |last=Haake }}</ref>

[[Roberto Heras]] and [[Primož Roglič]] hold the record for most victories with four. Heras's win in [[2005 Vuelta a España|2005]] was subject to a successful appeal in court, which overturned his initial disqualification for EPO in the 2005 race.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cyclingnews.com/news/heras-sues-for-one-million-euros |title=Heras sues for one million euros |work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=13 December 2013 |access-date=21 May 2020 |first=Peter |last=Cossins }}</ref> [[Alberto Contador]] and [[Tony Rominger]] have won three times. [[Angelino Soler]] is the youngest winner of the Vuelta at 21 years and 168 days old when he won in 1961. [[Chris Horner]] is the oldest winner of the Vuelta, winning the 2013 edition at the age of 41 years and 328 days old.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.procyclingstats.com/race/vuelta-a-espana/2021/gc/history/youngest-and-oldest-winners |title=Youngest and oldest winners of the Vuelta a España |publisher=Pro Cycling Stats |access-date=11 September 2022 }}</ref> Spanish cyclists have won the most Vueltas; 23 cyclists have won 32 Vueltas between them. French cyclists are second with nine victories and Belgian riders are third with eight wins.<ref name="autobus">{{cite news|url=http://autobus.cyclingnews.com/road/2008/vuelta08/?id=/features/2008/vuelta08_az2 |title=Vuelta a España O–Z  |work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=8 September 2008 |access-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref> The current champion is [[Enric Mas]] of {{UCI team code|MOV men|2026}}, who won the [[2026 Vuelta a España]].<ref name=jonas>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cycling/articles/cwyzglxlr6vo |title=Brennan misses record as Mas clinches Vuelta crown |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 September 2026 |access-date=13 September 2026 }}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Contador2.jpg|thumb|upright|alt=A man riding a bike in a gold top wearing a helmet and sunglasses|[[Alberto Contador]] in the gold jersey, which was replaced by a [[red jersey]] for 2010, representing the leader in the general classification.]]
The Vuelta a España was established in 1935 by the newspaper ''Informaciones'' following on from the success of the [[Tour de France]] and [[Giro d'Italia]] which had also been established by newspapers.<ref name="autobus" /> The first race was won by [[Gustaaf Deloor]], who won again the following year.<ref name="cyclingnews">{{cite news|url=http://autobus.cyclingnews.com/road/2008/vuelta08/?id=/features/2008/vuelta08_az1 |title=Vuelta a España A–N  |work=Cycling News |publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=7 September 2008 |access-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref> The Vuelta was suspended for four years from 1937 to 1940 due to the [[Spanish Civil War]]. The first race after the civil war in [[1941 Vuelta a España|1941]] was won by [[Julián Berrendero]], who also won the following year. The Vuelta was suspended between 1943 and 1944 due to the [[Second World War]]. [[Delio Rodríguez]] won the first Vuelta after the war, Spanish riders won two more Vueltas in [[1946 Vuelta a España|1946]] and [[1948 Vuelta a España|1948]]. The Vuelta was not held in 1949. [[Emilio Rodríguez (cyclist)|Emilio Rodríguez]] was the victor in [[1950 Vuelta a España|1950]], before the Vuelta was suspended from 1951 to 1954 as [[Francoist Spain|Spain's]] isolation during this period led to dwindling international interest in the race.<ref name="autobus" />

[[Jean Dotto]] won the first Vuelta after the four-year suspension in [[1955 Vuelta a España|1955]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1955 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908015723/http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1955 |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 September 2010 |title=Año 1955 |work=Vuelta a España |publisher=Unipublic |language=es |access-date=22 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Angelo Conterno]] was the victor the following year, by a margin of 13 seconds over [[Jesús Loroño]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1956 |title=Año 1956 |work=Vuelta a España |publisher=Unipublic |language=es |access-date=22 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908015728/http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1956 |archive-date=8 September 2010 }}</ref> Loroño was victorious in [[1957 Vuelta a España|1957]] with Conterno absent.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1957 |title=Año 1957 |work=Vuelta a España |publisher=Unipublic |language=es |access-date=22 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908015733/http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1957 |archive-date=8 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Rudi Altig]] became the first German to win the Vuelta in [[1962 Vuelta a España|1962]]. Frenchman [[Jacques Anquetil]] won in [[1963 Vuelta a España|1963]], in doing so he became the first cyclist to win all three Grand Tours.<ref>{{harvtxt|Howard|2011|p=13 }}</ref> Belgian cyclist [[Eddy Merckx]] matched Anquetil's achievement in winning all three Grand Tours when he won the Vuelta in [[1973 Vuelta a España|1973]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Fotheringham|2012|pp=213–14}}</ref> The following year [[José Manuel Fuente]] won the Vuelta by 11 seconds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1974 |title=Año 1974 |work=Vuelta a España |publisher=Unipublic |language=es |access-date=21 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100908015901/http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/anio.asp?a=1974 |archive-date=8 September 2010 }}</ref>

[[Bernard Hinault]] won the Vuelta in [[1978 Vuelta a España|1978]], a year in which he also won the Tour de France. He won his second Vuelta in [[1983 Vuelta a España|1983]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/hinault_bernard.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031004102429/http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/hinault_bernard.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 October 2003 |title=Bernard Hinault |publisher=Memoire du cyclisme |language=fr |access-date=21 September 2010 }}</ref> The following year [[Éric Caritoux]] won the Vuelta by the smallest margin ever, he won by six seconds over [[Alberto Fernández (cyclist)|Alberto Fernández]].<ref name="cyclingnews" /> [[Pedro Delgado]] won the Vuelta in [[1985 Vuelta a España|1985]]. Colombian [[Luis Herrera (cyclist)|Luis Herrera]] became the first non-European winner of the Vuelta in [[1987 Vuelta a España|1987]].<ref name="autobus" /> [[Sean Kelly (cyclist)|Sean Kelly]] was victorious in [[1988 Vuelta a España|1988]],<ref name="cyclingnews" /> and the following year Delgado won his second Vuelta.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/delgado_pedro.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031004030253/http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/delgado_pedro.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 October 2003 |title=Pedro Delgado |publisher=Memoire du cyclisme |language=fr |access-date=1 May 2011 }}</ref>

Swiss riders dominated the 1990s; [[Tony Rominger]] won a record three Vueltas in succession from [[1992 Vuelta a España|1992]] to [[1994 Vuelta a España|1994]].<ref name="autobus" /> [[Laurent Jalabert]] was victorious in [[1995 Vuelta a España|1995]], he also won the points and mountain classification becoming only the third person to win all these classifications in a single Grand Tour.<ref name="cyclingnews" /> [[Alex Zülle]] won two Vueltas in succession in [[1996 Vuelta a España|1996]] and [[1997 Vuelta a España|1997]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/zulle_alex.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050117051528/http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/zulle_alex.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 January 2005 |title=Alex Zülle |publisher=Memoire du cyclisme |language=fr |access-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref> German [[Jan Ullrich]] was the victor in [[1999 Vuelta a España|1999]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/ullrich_jan.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930181326/http://www.memoire-du-cyclisme.net/palmares/ullrich_jan.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 September 2007 |title=Jan Ullrich |publisher=Memoire du cyclisme |language=fr |access-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Roberto Heras]] won his first Vuelta in [[2000 Vuelta a España|2000]]; he won a further two in [[2003 Vuelta a España|2003]] and [[2004 Vuelta a España|2004]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/cycling/3691908.stm |title=Heras claims third Vuelta |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2004 |access-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref> In [[2005 Vuelta a España|2005]] he appeared to have won a record fourth Vuelta, however he was later stripped of his title after failing a drug-control test. Second place [[Denis Menchov]] became the victor.<ref name="Heras">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/cycling/4471264.stm |title=Heras contests two year drug ban |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 February 2005 |access-date=19 September 2010 }}</ref>

[[File:Primoz Roglic. Vuelta ciclista a Eapaña 2020. Alto de la Garganta de Baños de Montemayor. (50576911892).jpg|thumb|left|[[Primož Roglič]] wearing the red jersey during the [[2020 Vuelta a España]]]]
[[Alexander Vinokourov]] won the [[2006 Vuelta a España]] with the {{UCI team code|ONC|2006d}} team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2007/jul/25/howvinokourovwasbloodedint |title=How Vinokourov was blooded into the Tour of infamy |work=The Guardian |date=25 July 2007 |access-date=19 September 2010 |first=William |last=Fotherington }}</ref> Menchov won his second tour in [[2007 Vuelta a España|2007]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSL1990754120080219 |title=Menchov targets Tour rather than Vuelta defense |work=Reuters |date=19 February 2008 |access-date=19 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Alberto Contador]] won the [[2008 Vuelta a España|2008]] Vuelta; the victory meant he became the fifth cyclist to win all three Grand Tours.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclingweekly.co.uk/news/Contador_quickest_to_complete_grand_tour_set_article_268244.html |title=Contador quickest to complete Grand Tour set |last=Birnie |first=Lionel |author-link=Lionel Birnie |date=21 September 2008 |publisher=Cycling Weekly |access-date=19 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081024143946/http://www.cyclingweekly.co.uk/news/Contador_quickest_to_complete_grand_tour_set_article_268244.html |archive-date=24 October 2008 }}</ref> [[Alejandro Valverde]] was the victor in [[2009 Vuelta a España|2009]]. The following year, Valverde was unable to defend his title after being suspended for two years for his involvement in the [[Operación Puerto doping case]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/cycling/8714694.stm |title=Alejandro Valverde given two-year global doping ban |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 May 2010 |access-date=19 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Vincenzo Nibali]] won the [[2010 Vuelta a España|2010]] Vuelta.<ref name="Nibali">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/cycling/9013890.stm |title=Mark Cavendish wins historic Tour of Spain sprint title |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 September 2010 |access-date=19 September 2010 }}</ref> [[Juan José Cobo]] won the [[2011 Vuelta a España]] by thirteen seconds.<ref name="Cobo">{{cite news|url=http://www.cyclingnews.com/races/vuelta-a-espana-2011/stage-21/results |title=Sagan steals final stage from pure sprinters |work=Cycling News|publisher=Future Publishing Limited |date=11 September 2011|author=Les Clarke|access-date=19 September 2011 }}</ref>  However, on 12 June 2019, the UCI announced that Cobo was found guilty of an anti-doping rule violation in relation to his biological passport and stripped of his title six days later. Runner-up [[Chris Froome]] was awarded the win to retrospectively become the first British cyclist to win a Grand Tour.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/49026538 |title=Chris Froome awarded 2011 Vuelta a Espana as Juan Jose Cobo stripped of title |website=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2019 |access-date=21 May 2020 }}</ref>

Contador won his second Vuelta in [[2012 Vuelta a España|2012]].<ref name="Contador #2">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/19537111 |title=Alberto Contador wins second Vuelta a Espana title |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 September 2012 |access-date=19 September 2012 }}</ref> American [[Chris Horner]], became the oldest Grand Tour winner at the age of 41, when he won the Vuelta in [[2013 Vuelta a España|2013]].<ref name="Horner">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/24101494 |title=Vuelta a Espana: Chris Horner, 41, is oldest Grand Tour winner |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 September 2013 |access-date=17 September 2013 }}</ref> Contador won the race for the third time in [[2014 Vuelta a España|2014]], as he beat [[Chris Froome]] by one minute and ten seconds.<ref name=espana>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/29200614 |title=Vuelta a Espana:Alberto Contador beat Chris Froome |website=BBC Sport |date=14 September 2014 |access-date=31 May 2014 }}</ref> Fabio Aru beat [[Tom Dumoulin]] by 57 seconds in 2015 to win the Vuelta.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/34239346 |title=Vuelta a Espana: Italian Fabio Aru wins first Grand Tour title |website=BBC Sport |date=13 September 2015 |access-date=21 May 2016 }}</ref>  [[Nairo Quintana]] won the 2016 Vuelta, one minute and twenty-three seconds ahead of Froome.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/sep/11/chris-froome-nairo-quintana-vuelta-a-espana |title=Nairo Quintana resists Chris Froome challenge to win Vuelta a España |work=The Guardian |date=11 September 2016 |access-date=21 May 2020 }}</ref> Froome was successful the following year to become the first rider since Hinault in 1978 to win the Tour and Vuelta in the same year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/sep/10/chris-froome-wins-vuelta-a-espana-2017 |title=Chris Froome seals Vuelta a España title to win historic Vuelta-Tour double |work=The Guardian |date=10 September 2017 |access-date=21 May 2020 |first=William |last=Fotheringham }}</ref> [[Simon Yates (cyclist)|Simon Yates]] won the 2018 Vuelta. It was the third victory by a British rider in a Grand Tour in 2018 and the first time three different riders from the same country had won all three races in one year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/sep/16/simon-yates-victory-gives-britain-grand-slam-cycling-triumph |title=Simon Yates's Vuelta victory crowns a stunning year for British cycling |work=The Guardian |date=16 September 2018 |access-date=21 May 2020 |first=Sam |last=Jones }}</ref> [[Primož Roglič]] won the 2019 Vuelta to become the first Slovenian rider to win a Grand Tour.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/sep/15/vuelta-2019-primoz-roglic-wins-first-grand-tour-fabio-jakobsen |title=Primoz Roglic seals Vuelta a España triumph as race ends in Madrid |work=The Guardian |date=15 September 2019 |access-date=21 May 2020 }}</ref> Roglič won again the following year, beating runner-up [[Richard Carapaz]] by 24 seconds.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/54859001 |title=Hugh Carthy seals Vuelta a Espana podium as Primoz Roglic wins red jersey |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 November 2020 |access-date=8 November 2020 |first=Matt |last=Warwick }}</ref> Roglič became the first rider since Heras to win three consecutive Vueltas, when he won the 2021 edition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/sep/05/primoz-roglic-wins-final-stage-to-take-third-vuelta-a-espana-title |title=Primoz Roglic wins final stage to take third Vuelta a España title |work=The Guardian |date=5 September 2021 |access-date=5 September 2021 }}</ref> [[Remco Evenepoel]] won the [[2022 Vuelta a España]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cycling/62871067 |title=Vuelta a Espana: Belgium's Remco Evenepoel seals maiden Grand Tour win |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 September 2022 |access-date=11 September 2022 }}</ref> [[Sepp Kuss]] won the [[2023 Vuelta a España|2023 Vuelta]] by 17 seconds from his teammate [[Jonas Vingegaard]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cycling/66839092 |title=Vuelta a Espana: Sepp Kuss wins 2023 race as Kaden Groves claims final stage |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 September 2023 |access-date=18 September 2023 }}</ref> Roglič won the Vuelta the following year to equal Heras's record for most victories with four.<ref name=primoz>{{cite news|url=https://www.cyclingnews.com/races/vuelta-a-espana-2024/stage-21/results/ |title=Vuelta a España: Primož Roglič claims fourth GC title as Stefan Küng wins stage 21 time trial |work=Cycling News |date=8 September 2024 |access-date=8 September 2024 |first=Lyne |last=Lamoureux }}</ref> [[Jonas Vingegaard]] won the Vuelta the following year.<ref name=jonas />

! scope="row" |{{sortname|Roberto|Heras}}{{efn|[[Roberto Heras]] was the winner at the podium ceremony in Madrid on the last day of the [[2005 Vuelta a España]], but subsequently was found to have tested positive for performance-enhancing drugs during stage 20 of the race. The Spanish cycling federation found him guilty of using [[erythropoietin]] during the race and stripped him of his title, awarding the win to [[Denis Menchov]].<ref name="Heras" />  However, in 2012 Roberto Heras was reinstated as the 2005 Vuelta a España champion when Spain's supreme court ruled in favor of Heras, citing procedural violations relating to the storage and handling of the urine samples.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclingweekly.co.uk/news/racing/vuelta-a-espana/roberto-heras-regains-2005-vuelta-a-espana-win-35724 |title=Roberto Heras regains 2005 Vuelta a Espana win |date=24 December 2012 |publisher=Cycling Weekly |access-date=14 February 2017 }}</ref>}}
